name: BMP-2

image.license: See Commons file page for license

cost.display: Legacy Soviet stock, 20,000+ built historically - no current market price

characteristics: Strength: Autocannon gives more direct-fire punch than BMP-1's low-velocity gun; huge legacy fleet size
Limitation: Thin armor (33mm max) even by 1980s standards, now especially vulnerable to top-attack drone munitions
Estimated quantity available: Legacy stock in the low thousands pre-war; current operational count reduced by heavy attrition
employment_notes: Still forms a large share of Russia's IFV fleet by sheer numbers despite its age, illustrating the broader pattern of legacy Soviet armor absorbing most of the war's attrition
contrast_vs_traditional: Soviet mechanized doctrine sent BMP columns forward together, expecting artillery to suppress the column as a single target. FPVs don't work that way — each vehicle in the column is now an individually identified, individually engaged target, which is the same shift from massed to distributed engagement doctrine.md describes happening down to squad level on the infantry side.
